description: PDF-derived Markdown of the public August 2025 City of Richfield, Minnesota stormwater model update and flood-risk prioritization study, drafted into an eight-section Minnesota DNR Flood Hazard Mitigation application.

source.provenance: Mistral OCR (mistral-ocr-latest) of the public Barr Engineering report, assembled with CityCatalyst page-marker, header/footer, and table rules. The certifying engineer, licence number, and private email correspondents are redacted.

facts.statement: The stormwater model covers the entire City of Richfield and the adjacent areas that drain into Richfield.

evidence.text: The model covers the entire city and the areas of adjacent cities that drain into Richfield.

facts.statement: Barr updated the PCSWMM model with LiDAR data collected in 2022 and published by the USGS.

evidence.text: Barr updated the existing PCSWMM model to incorporate the Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data collected in 2022 and published by the United States Geological Survey (USGS)

facts.statement: The updated model simulates four design storm events, including the climate-adaptation MCE100-year event, using the MSE3 rainfall distribution.

evidence.text: The four design storm events use the Midwest Southeast 3 (MSE3) rainfall distribution
The PCSWMM model was used to simulate four design rainfall events.

facts.statement: Flood-risk areas were scored on storm system conditions, critical infrastructure, frequency of flooding, social vulnerability index, and number of flood-prone structures.

evidence.text:
The criteria selected to score the flood-risk areas are:

- Storm system conditions
- Critical infrastructure
- Frequency of flooding
- Social vulnerability index (SVI)
- Number of flood-prone structures

facts.statement: 746 flood-risk areas were evaluated, 601 of them within or primarily within the municipal boundary.

evidence.text: A total of 746 flood-risk areas were evaluated from the study area with 601 flood-risk areas located within or primarily within the municipal boundary.

facts.statement: The city selected three flood-risk areas, for which six mitigation concepts were identified and evaluated in the updated model.

evidence.text: Three flood-risk areas were selected by the city based on the project prioritization framework developed. For these three flood-risk areas a total of six mitigation concepts were identified and evaluated in the updated stormwater model.
The prioritization by flood-risk area was reviewed by city staff who identified three locations for a planning-level evaluation.

facts.statement: The selected flood-risk areas are near Wilson Pond, northwest of Roosevelt Park, and near Woodlawn Terrace.

evidence.text: The area around Wilson Pond is one of the locations with the largest risk of flooding in the city.
The flood-risk area Northwest of Roosevelt Park was selected by the city for further evaluation.
The flood-risk area near Woodlawn Terrace was selected by the city for further evaluation.

facts.statement: The Section 5 projects, model results, and cost estimates are concept-level designs.

evidence.text: The projects, model results, and cost estimates presented in Section 5 are represent a concept level design.
Based on the concept level design, a planning-level cost estimate was developed for city staff to consider when planning for further evaluation of each project.

facts.statement: All costs are presented in 2025 US dollars with an accuracy range of -30% to +50%.

evidence.text: All costs are presented in 2025 US dollars.
Note: Total project cost accuracy range is -30% to +50%.

facts.statement: Concept cost estimates range from $1,540,000 near Woodlawn Terrace to $17,333,000 for Wilson Pond Concept C.
The model study area is approximately 8.8 square miles.

evidence.text: The model study area covers the total watershed area included in the H&H model which is approximately 8.8 square miles

facts.statement: The applicant is the City of Richfield, Minnesota.
The application targets the Minnesota DNR Flood Hazard Mitigation Grant Assistance Program.
Richfield has a recorded population of 36,994.
746 flood-risk areas were evaluated, 601 within or primarily within the municipal boundary.
The project addresses the flood-risk areas near Wilson Pond, northwest of Roosevelt Park, and near Woodlawn Terrace.
At Wilson Pond the lowest structures are affected during the 2-year 24-hour rainfall event.
The concept cost estimates are carried into the funding or financing sections.
Costs are stated in 2025 US dollars.
Cost estimates carry a -30% to +50% accuracy range.
Surface storage and underground storage near Wilson Pond were ruled out because of space and shallow groundwater.
The selected areas lie in parts of the city with a high social vulnerability index.
